title: Probe priority weighting and feedback-driven traffic shedder for cohort-aware canary probes
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We observed that canary probe budgets are inefficient during heterogeneous traffic surges: low-impact cohorts consume probes while a handful of high-impact cohorts drive tail latency and business impact. This PR introduces two complementary changes: 1) a probe importance weighting system that scores cohorts by impact (cohort impact score = traffic share * weighted tail-latency sensitivity) and reassigns probe budget dynamically, and 2) a feedback-driven Traffic Shedder that applies lightweight backpressure to low-impact cohorts when the serving tier detects sustained overload, preserving probe coverage for critical cohorts and protecting SLOs.

This is an operational-facing change intended to improve detection fidelity for regressions that matter to customers and reduce false positives/noisy alerts from low-impact slices. The changes are conservative by default (feature-flagged) and include safety ramps: global ramp percentage, per-cohort minimum probe floor, and a gradual shed rate limiter.

Implementation highlights:
- probe_scheduler: new priority weighting module (scheduler/probe_priority.go) that computes cohort impact scores using a configurable formula and exposes a probe allocation API.
- canary_prober: reworked allocation loop to request budgets from the scheduler and to emit cohort-weighted metrics (weighted_p50/p95/throughput) for the canary evaluator.
- traffic_shedder: new component (runtime/traffic_shedder.go) that implements a feedback loop using moving-window overload detection + token-bucket-based shedder per cohort; integrates with smart routing to set short-lived rate limits.
- routing: small hooks to accept per-cohort temporary limits and fallback rules.
- console: dashboard tile and a diagnostic table for cohort impact score, active shed rates, and probe weight history.

Checklist:
- [x] Core scheduler algorithm implemented and unit-tested
- [x] Traffic Shedder runtime and integration tests
- [x] Feature flag + config surface documented in console and config reference
- [x] Canary evaluator updated to consume weighted metrics and report drift alerts
- [x] Load test harness scenario added to perf-canary lab (traffic shape: bursty heterogeneous cohorts)
- [x] Rollout plan: gated behind a runtime flag; start with 1% of accounts and monitor weighted_p95 regressions

Why different from prior work: Prior canary work focused primarily on detection algorithms and baseline adjustments. This diff shifts probe economy to prioritize cohorts by business/technical impact and pairs it with an active feedback mechanism to conserve resources under overload. It reduces noisy canary churn and improves detection fidelity where it matters most.

Notes: The scoring formula is pluggable; we ship an initial heuristic (traffic_share * (0.7 * p95_z + 0.3 * failure_rate_z)). We evaluated sensitivity in the perf lab and included a conservative default config.
commits_summary: 4 commits: initial priority-weighting prototype and scheduler tests; add token-bucket traffic shedder and integration points; wire console metrics and dashboards; add docs, config and load-test scenarios. Each commit is focused and includes unit/integration tests where applicable.
review_comments: Diego Alvarez (2026-01-18): Nice approach. Two questions: how do we avoid starving new cohorts that don't yet have p95 history? Also, can we expose an emergency kill switch for the shedder?

Maya Chen (author) (2026-01-18): We added a per-cohort minimum probe floor and bootstrap smoothing so new cohorts inherit a small default weight until they accumulate stats. Also added a runtime emergency kill switch (config flag) and a console action to toggle it. See runtime/traffic_shedder.go lines 110-140.

Priya Nadar (2026-01-21): Can we make the scoring weights configurable per org? Some customers want failure-rate prioritized.
Requested change: add org-level overrides to config lookup.
Maya Chen (2026-01-22): Implemented org-level overrides via the config service with fallback to cluster defaults. Added tests for override precedence.
Ethan Cole (2026-01-25): Minor nit: clarify units on the dashboard tile and add a tooltip explaining the scoring formula. Also saw a flaky test on CI (TestTrafficShedderBurst) — rerun needed.
Maya Chen (2026-01-26): Added tooltip and clarified units. Fixed race in test by using a synthetic clock; reran CI — transient flake resolved.
ci_checks: perf-lab: added new scenario but not blocking on CI (manual perf runs completed)
merge_outcome_note: Merged after approvals and CI green. Feature gated; rollout started at 1% of accounts with monitoring dashboards and alerting on weighted_p95 deviation.
release_notes: Introduce cohort-priority probe weighting and a feedback-driven Traffic Shedder to improve canary probe economy and reduce noisy regressions. Configurable, feature-flagged, and includes org-level overrides. Not enabled by default.
